purpose.summary: Connect the canonical node-storage transaction reader to the accepted Chronik token runtime through a bounded C++/Rust bridge and build the confirmed Tx protobuf.
scope: Resolve the accepted transaction block identity and bind the node-supplied body, coinbase role and spent coins.
Preserve upstream ALP and SLP token conversion and canonical Chronik protobuf field layouts.
Bound input and response sizes, contain Rust panics, and require a sizing probe followed by a checked buffer copy.
Exercise real C++/Rust calls, ALP ancestry annotations and fail-closed contradiction and rollback behavior.
exclusions: No transaction HTTP route, spent-by lookup, mempool, history, UTXO, websocket, plugin or wallet surface is added.
No consensus, validation, activation, chain-selection, P2P, network identity or mainnet parameter change.
No duplicate transaction-body store, private history, operator material, incoming evidence, cache, binary or host-specific path is tracked.

commands: Configure the standalone node with BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=OFF and inspect the generated bitcoind build graph.
expected_results: The confirmed transaction bridge and reader are absent from the compiled-out build graph.

commands: Build test_bitcoin and bitcoind with BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=ON while leaving runtime observer opt-in disabled.
expected_results: The C++/Rust bridge compiles with no new database, socket or runtime activation when disabled.

commands: Run the runtime and observer Rust tests offline from the committed Cargo.lock, then the focused chronik_confirmed_tx_bridge_tests and existing reader/envelope suites.
expected_results: Canonical ALP token annotations, block identity binding, coinbase/spent-coin roles, bounded ABI and rollback failures pass.

scenarios.command: Run chronik_confirmed_tx_bridge_tests and the existing explicit local-regtest observer scenarios against the observer-enabled native build.
expected_results: Four bridge tests and 27 assertions pass, including the fail-closed identity and undo cases, while observer opt-in remains explicit.
failure_conditions: Wrong transaction selection, missing or misaligned spent coin accepted, identity contradiction accepted, implicit observer state, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run the existing restart scenario and repeat the focused bridge unit suite in separate fresh processes.
expected_results: Restart reconstruction remains stable and the bridge preserves exact transaction and spent-coin selection.
failure_conditions: Reconstruction drift, reader regression, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run the existing full-reindex observer scenario with the compiled bridge present.
expected_results: The accepted index rebuilds without changing node validation or invoking an unregistered transaction route.
failure_conditions: Stale state, node-authority effect, unexpected route, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run the existing chainstate-reindex observer scenario with the compiled bridge present.
expected_results: Ordered callbacks rebuild queryable state while the bridge remains a passive node-storage adapter.
failure_conditions: Stale state, validation effect, unexpected route, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run the existing pruned-datadir observer scenario and retain the bridge's unavailable-data failure law.
expected_results: Unavailable historical blk or rev data fails the read and cannot affect node correctness.
failure_conditions: Partial transaction result, node shutdown, validation effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run the existing deep-reorganization scenario and the bridge identity-contradiction unit cases.
expected_results: Observer contradictions remain isolated and an active-chain identity change cannot produce a silent orphan transaction result.
failure_conditions: Orphan result, stale observer state, node-authority effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

limitations: No transaction HTTP route exists yet. The caller must serialize lookup/read/encode against accepted-index mutations and govern the active-chain reorganization boundary before a future response.
This confirmed-only protobuf leaves spent_by absent, plugin maps empty and finalization false. Missing spent_by does not imply an unspent output.
The node remains responsible for canonical transaction bodies and spent coins; historical blk/rev availability is required by the prior reader.
Input transaction bytes, aggregate spent scripts and encoded responses each have a 64 MiB bound; there are at most one million spent coins.
Local component tests do not establish independent reproduction, production deployment, full Chronik API compatibility or consensus activation.
counterevidence: A canonical transaction response cannot be reconstructed when the node has pruned the relevant body or undo data; the bridge provides no duplicate-store fallback.
An output without spent_by is intentionally incomplete and cannot be used as an unspentness assertion.
Separate sizing and copy calls alone do not provide a reorganization snapshot; external serialization remains mandatory before route integration.
